claim: GMP certification means an independent auditor assessed the manufacturer's quality management system — it does NOT mean FDA approval of the product.
stance_target: GMP certification is a quality-system signal, not a product safety guarantee
scope_conditions: U.S. dietary supplement market; applicable globally as conceptual framework
quoted_support: GMP certified supplements usually means a supplement brand claims an independent party audited its manufacturing system against GMP expectations. Importantly, GMP certification does not mean 'FDA approved.'

claim: 57.6% of U.S. adults reported using a dietary supplement in the last 30 days, and FDA has identified over 1,000 tainted products with hidden drug ingredients.
stance_target: Supplement quality verification matters at consumer scale
quoted_support: In the U.S. alone, 57.6% of adults reported using a dietary supplement in the last 30 days. However, FDA also warns that some products contain hidden drug ingredients, and it has identified over a thousand tainted products in recent years.

claim: GMP-compliant (self-claimed) and GMP-certified (third-party audited) are distinct: self-claim has no external audit proof whereas certification provides a certificate with scope, site, dates, and certifier identity.
stance_target: Third-party GMP certification is more credible than self-declared GMP compliance
quoted_support: GMP compliant (self-claim): The company says it follows GMP rules. [Proof:] Internal SOPs, maybe a COA; often no public audit proof. Third-party GMP certification: An auditor assessed the facility/system against a standard. [Proof:] Certificate with scope, site, dates, and certifier identity.

claim: GMP certification focuses on production processes (supplier qualification, ingredient testing, batch records, hygiene, in-process checks, finished product release) but does not certify product efficacy or exact dosage delivery.
stance_target: GMP certification scope and limitations for consumer evaluation
scope_conditions: Dietary supplement manufacturing per FDA 21 CFR Part 111
quoted_support: GMP supports supplement quality, but it does not prove clinical effectiveness or FDA approval.
